_comment: Optional control-state. Copy to config.json and pass with --config. Every field is optional; omitted fields fall back to the built-in defaults (which reproduce the source workbook). The two DATA files (inventory + sales) are passed on the command line, not here.
_suppress_comment: Discontinued / no-longer-orderable combos. A bare code drops the whole trim; add ext/int to target one. Suppressed combos never appear as an order suggestion, but their on-lot/incoming units still count and still show in overstock.
_roster_add_comment: Extra orderable combos the built-in roster doesn't carry (new trims/colors). Uses the DMS 4-digit code + ext + int.
_prev_loaners_comment: Units back from demo duty. 'taken'/'returned' are when it left and re-entered sellable stock; the engine subtracts only that hidden demo stretch from days-in-stock (real market time = DMS - days out) and never wholesale-lists it (miles). 'note' = driver/reason.
_trades_comment: Outbound dealer trades. Each is a sale out the other door; 'days' is days-in-stock at trade (grades speed to enter/exit inventory). date drives recency (R90/R180).
_loaner_comment: Courtesy-vehicle (ICV) program, done as three math problems: (1) true cost per combo = invoice; (2) used value = what a comparable current/1-MY-old unit sells for, modeled until real data as preowned_price_pct (~0.80) x the CHEAPEST NEW price, where cheapest-new = invoice - rebates[model]; (3) the write-downs (one-time ICV + monthly write-down + velocity bonus) reduce the preowned cost basis only when the unit retires from the fleet, and preowned_gross = used value - adjusted cost tells you if the resale profits or is upside down (cost above street/auction value). 'loaner_units' are pulled from sellable inventory like demos. 'preowned_sales' (optional) hold your own used sales and/or public wholesale/auction comps and override the 80% model.
